title.narrative: Health Recovery in North East Syria Project (HERNES 2)

description.narrative: The approach is two-pronged. On the one hand, and to secure the achievements reached by HERNES 1, the project intends to continue to support the delivery of basic health services, as well as maternity care in the 7 facilities currently supported.On the other hand, EF intends to further contribute to lay the foundation for a more durable recovery of the health sector in the NES. This will be achieved through ensuring that the work that is performed in the supported centers can form the basis for a greater harmonization and coordination of practices, protocols and guidelines. To this purpose, EF will provide technical assistance to the Health Working Group under the NES in the fields of Reproductive Maternal Newborn and Child Health (RMNCH) and Supply Chain Management. EF also intends to support NES health actors policy dialogue on the recovery and future prospects of a stabilized and functioning health system in Syria and strengthen its support to capacity building through trainings of and support to health workers.

title.narrative: Number of people trained by the EUfunded intervention who increased their knowledge of and/or skills in following sustainable land and water management practices (disaggregated by sex, age and population group)

description.narrative: The United Nations defines sustainable land management (SLM) as the use of land resources, including soils, water, animals and plants, for the production of goods to meet changing human needs, while simultaneously ensuring the longterm productive potential of these resources and the maintenance of their environmental functions. This indicator measures how many people have been trained in sustainable land and water management practices.If monitoring capacity is limited or the context is fragile, this indicator could be simplified to monitor only the number of persons trained (without referring to an increase in knowledge and/or skills). However, in order to ensure the quality of training and the achievement of the desired result, it is recommended to assess the knowledge of participants before and after the intervention whenever possible.
